owner_summary.title: Finance / Public Money pilot
what_changed: Sixteen private public-money records now connect official funding evidence to ten Miller and six Miller North chains.
Thirty-two financial evidence edges distinguish program, recipient, service and operational-result traceability.
Four canonical cross-domain fixtures are ready for regression validation, not publication.
owner_summary.why_it_matters: The Farm can now show what was funded, who was named, and what service or institution can actually be demonstrated without allocating broad envelopes to individual resources.
strongest_evidence: New Roads has a named $4.39-million service-level announcement, recipient and later operating-service evidence.
FNHO has distinct First Nations governance, $1.17-million establishment funding, later $775,000 recipient funding and current operation.
Health Canada's register names recipient, amount and project scope for AVI, Providence and Kílala Lelum prescribed-alternatives projects.
uncertainty: Road to Recovery and Budget 2023 amounts remain program-level and cannot be allocated to named sites.
Overlapping announcements and project extensions must not be summed without agreement reconciliation.
The St. Paul's curriculum project has confirmed funding but no later completion source located.
Health-authority audited statements rarely expose selected-service allocations.
owner_summary.recommended_next_move: Owner-review the four canonical fixtures, then verify the St. Paul's curriculum completion and reconcile one CMHA BC provider-level bed allocation before expanding the lane.

pass_owner_summary.title: Canonical fixtures and public-money consolidation
what_changed: Four cross-domain records were formalized as private canonical regression fixtures.
A focused In Plain Sight review separated six specifically evidenced recommendations from the current 24-recommendation reporting gap.
The new public-money lane validated 16 records and 32 evidence-bearing financial relationships.
The official-source registry expanded from 27 to 29 families.
pass_owner_summary.why_it_matters: Future Farm runs now have trusted examples for policy-to-resource, funding-to-service, Indigenous governance and accountability-reporting validation, plus a conservative financial trace model that stops where public attribution stops.
strongest_evidence: New Roads links a stated $4.39-million service amount to a named recipient and operating program.
FNHO preserves Chiefs-in-Assembly governance separately from federal establishment and continuation funding.
B.C.'s current Action 3.07 page itself documents both implementation activity and limited comprehensive reporting across all 24 recommendations.
uncertainty: Twelve of 16 funding records remain owner-gated, chiefly because amounts are program-level, overlap, or lack later output evidence.
No current comprehensive official status ledger covering all 24 In Plain Sight recommendations was located.
Procurement and audited statements usually require separate operational evidence before a resource link is safe.
pass_owner_summary.recommended_next_move: Approve the four fixtures for private regression use, then complete one provider-level CMHA bed allocation and the St. Paul's curriculum follow-up as the next two finance-lane tests.

research_brief.title: Tracing Public Funding to Addiction and Indigenous Health Services: A Private Farm Research Pilot
research_brief.executive_summary: A 16-record pilot tested whether public funding announcements and disclosures could be traced to recipients, services and later operational evidence across Miller and Miller North. Four records reached service-level funding confirmation, while broad budgets and health-authority totals generally stopped at program or organization level.
research_brief.scope: Ten British Columbia/federal addictions funding records and six Indigenous-health accountability or governance funding records were selected from existing private chains. Official budgets, announcements, grant disclosures, health-authority reporting, Indigenous-organization reporting and implementation sources were preferred.
key_findings: Named grants and contribution agreements produced the cleanest recipient-to-service traces.
Road to Recovery has strong implementation evidence but no authoritative site-level allocation of the $23.7-million annual or nearly $154-million expansion envelopes.
FNHO demonstrates why governance authority, funding source and operational control must be represented separately.
A funded curriculum announcement and an operational Alberta advocate role remain incomplete financial traces for different reasons.
Audited health-authority statements are valuable context but rarely prove service-level spending.
evidence_highlights: B.C. announced $4.39 million over three years for New Roads and later sources confirm the operating program.
Health Canada reports $6,065,479 for Kílala Lelum's prescribed-alternatives and Elder-led healing project.
ISC announced $1.17 million to establish FNHO; a later federal grant disclosure identifies a separate $775,000 agreement.
B.C. officially connects its $171.8-million Indigenous Fund to In Plain Sight recommendation 17 at program level.
policy_service_relationships: Road to Recovery commitment → program funding → health-authority implementation → operating service, with no site-level amount.
SUAP contribution → named recipient/project → described service delivery.
First Nations governance resolution → federal establishment funding → operating ombudsperson office.
In Plain Sight recommendation 17 → provincial Indigenous Fund → Indigenous-led service program, with recipient allocations unresolved.
research_brief.implementation_status: Five records reach service-level or network operational-result confirmation, six confirm funding only at program or recipient level, three carry explicit non-attribution boundaries, one funded output remains unverified, and one operating role lacks a public role-specific amount. These statuses do not evaluate adequacy or effectiveness.
unresolved_questions: Can a CMHA BC grant document map a specific bed allocation to a named Miller resource?
Was the St. Paul's cultural-safety curriculum completed and deployed in all three named platforms?
Can a current procurement or contract record establish the value of a selected contracted service without relying on supplier payments alone?
Which later audits report at the same program scope as the selected funding records?
research_brief.method: Existing private policy and accountability chains were screened for public-money relevance. Amount, recipient, purpose, scope and recurrence were recorded only when stated. Every relationship required an authoritative source; funding, operation, utilization and outcomes remained separate stages. No overlapping amounts were aggregated.
sources: B.C. budgets, estimates, news releases and ministry annual reports
Fraser, Vancouver Coastal, Island and Provincial Health Services Authority reporting
Health Canada funded-project registers and contribution announcements
Indigenous Services Canada funding announcements and Open Government grant disclosures
FNHA audited, annual and evaluation reporting; FNHO governance and annual reports
research_brief.limitations: The sample is purposive and private. Announcement values may be maximums or envelopes rather than expenditures. Audited entity statements generally lack service detail; supplier lists lack purpose; operational evidence does not establish effectiveness; and no value-for-money, wrongdoing or adequacy conclusion was attempted.
